edits.old: Percona's 2021 MongoDB 5.0 article describes automatic timeField indexing and an optional metaField, while MongoDB's manual dates the default metaField/timeField compound index to version 6.3; the default compound-index rule must therefore be scoped by release. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14)
edits.new: Percona's 2021 MongoDB 5.0 article describes automatic timeField indexing and an optional metaField, while MongoDB's manual dates the default metaField/timeField compound index to version 6.3; the default compound-index rule must therefore be scoped by release. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) Sources: https://www.percona.com/blog/mongodb-5-0-time-series-collections/ ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/timeseries/timeseries-index.md

evidence.quote: timeField: the name of the field where the date is stored. This will be automatically indexed and used for retrieving data.
It’s optional. It cannot be the _id or the same as the timeField.

Starting in MongoDB 6.3, MongoDB creates a default  [compound index](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-compound.md#std-label-index-type-compound) on both the metaField and timeField of a time series collection.

statements.statement: Percona's 2021 MongoDB 5.0 article describes automatic timeField indexing and an optional metaField
MongoDB's manual dates the default metaField/timeField compound index to version 6.3, so the rule must be scoped by release

edits.rationale: The Percona article (dated October 20, 2021) says the timeField is automatically indexed and the metaField is optional. The MongoDB manual says the default compound index on metaField and timeField starts in 6.3. The default-index rule is therefore version-scoped.

edits.old: MongoDB documents the default {metaField: 1, timeField: 1} compound index as new in 6.3, and the server README says it is created for new collections in 6.3 and later; operators should verify the index on collections created before that default existed. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14)
edits.new: MongoDB documents the default {metaField: 1, timeField: 1} compound index as new in 6.3, and the server's time-series README says it is created by default for new time series collections created in v6.3+; if the index does not exist, query-based bucket reopening is not used. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/timeseries/timeseries-index.md ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/mongo/master/src/mongo/db/timeseries/README.md

evidence.quote: Starting in MongoDB 6.3, MongoDB creates a default  [compound index](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-compound.md#std-label-index-type-compound) on both the metaField and timeField of a time series collection.

This index is created by default for new time series collections created in v6.3+. If
the index does not exist, then query-based reopening will not be used.

statements.statement: MongoDB documents the default {metaField:1, timeField:1} compound index as new in 6.3
The server README says it is created for new collections in 6.3 and later
statements.note: README says created by default for new time series collections created in v6.3+.

statements.statement: Operators should verify the index on collections created before that default existed
statements.note: Advice not stated by a source; the README says that without the index, query-based reopening is not used.

edits.rationale: The manual and the server README both support the 6.3 default and the new-collections scope. The 'operators should verify older collections' advice is not stated by a source, but the README says reopening is skipped without the index, so the corrected text states that instead.
